defect_LIFE_1.title: The client's automatic reconnect after a production logout is rejected whenever the character's save reconstructs a boat
defect_LIFE_1.symptom: osrs239 login: rejected reply=<n>, followed by the 'Connection lost / Please wait - attempting to reestablish' overlay that never clears.
defect_LIFE_1.why_it_looked_intermittent: <n> is not a login response code at all. Observed today on the shared binary: 16, 195, 209 (x4), 239. 195 is the value the handoff recorded. The value is a byte of ISAAC keystream, so it differs per session and reads like a flaky server.

what_195_means.answer: Nothing. It is not a LoginResponse.
what_195_means.evidence: src/net/rev/osrs239/loginblock.h defines the whole set: SUCCESSFUL 0, OK 2, INVALID_USER_OR_PASS 3, CLIENT_OUT_OF_DATE 6, BAD_SESSION_ID 10, RECONNECT_OK 15, INVALID_LOGIN_PACKET 22, LOGIN_FAIL_1 65, PROOF_OF_WORK 69. The server only ever writes OK (torirs_server_session.c:767) and RECONNECT_OK (torirs_server_encode.c:790). 195/209/239/16 are none of these.
what_195_means.what_the_client_actually_read: src/net/loginproto_osrs239.c:425 `int reply = h->in[0]` while the handle is in OSRS239_AWAIT_REPLY. The byte it read was the first byte of an ISAAC-scrambled GAME packet that the server had already written to the same stream.

root_cause.one_line: A reconnect's LoginResponse.ReconnectOk is deferred until after the save is read, but reading the save SENDS — a boat save runs the deck reconstruction, whose varbit writes reach the wire four or more packets ahead of the login response.
chain: torirs_server_session.c:712 — a GAMERECONNECT handshake sends NOTHING and only arms the ciphers; the response is deliberately deferred, because RECONNECT_OK carries the player-info init block and the block states where the save put the player.

torirs_server_world.c ToriRSServer_WorldLogin step -1 — ToriRSServer_LoadPlayer, then ToriRSServer_VesselLogin reconstructs the at-sea owned boat BEFORE the login scene/GPI coordinate is emitted (it has to: the player's coordinate is the deck tile).

That reconstruction runs vessel_deck_built -> ToriRSServer_VarbitSet -> ToriRSServer_WorldSetVarpOn -> ToriRSServer_WorldMarkVarp -> ToriRSServer_SendVarpSmall. Those are ordinary ISAAC-scrambled game packets.
torirs_server_world.c step 0b — only NOW is ToriRSServer_SendReconnectOk called. It is already behind the varps on the wire.
The client is still in OSRS239_AWAIT_REPLY, reads the first scrambled byte as the verdict, and dies.
root_cause.measured_with_TORIRSSERVER_VERBOSE_1: /tmp/sailing-fin-195a/client.log — 'reconnect user=f195a session=ok' at line 716, four '-> VARP_SMALL op=97 payload=3' sends at lines 737/738/754/771 (interleaved with the deck's LOC_ADD_CHANGE zone events and 'sailing_deck_built ran=1 handle=1 config=2'), then 'RECONNECT_OK, 4608 byte player-info init at 6404,67' at line 777, then 'osrs239 login: rejected reply=16' at line 781.
root_cause.the_control_that_names_it: An ASHORE save writes no varps in that window. /tmp/sailing-fin-lifecycle-login and /tmp/sailing-fin-lifecycle-sail2 both logged out ashore, both reconnected ('reconnect user=finlife session=ok'), and NEITHER produced a rejection line. Every aboard logout produced one.

defect_LIFE_1.user_visible_shape: This is not a --resume-save failure: a fresh --resume-save process always logs in cleanly (GAMELOGIN, LOGINRES_OK sent during the handshake, before any game packet). It is the LOGGED-OUT client's own auto-reconnect that dies, which is why the line lands at the tail of the previous session's log and looked as if it belonged to the next one. docs/sailing_validation/lifecycle-chat-after-logout.png is what a player sees.

fix.change: return early while `player->session && player->session->reconnect`. That flag is set by the GAMERECONNECT handshake and cleared in ToriRSServer_WorldLogin the instant ToriRSServer_SendReconnectOk returns, so it is exactly 'this client has not been told the login verdict yet'.
fix.why_nothing_is_lost: Step 4b of ToriRSServer_WorldLoginFinish already restates EVERY non-zero transmitted varp in full, precisely because the loader writes player->varps[] directly and marks nothing. The values held back are re-sent a few lines later by code that exists for this reason.
fix.scope_honestly_stated: This guard covers the varp writer, which is the only emitter measured in that window. The GENERAL guard belongs at the top of ToriRSServer_Send (src/torirsserver/torirs_server_encode.c) so that no future login-time writer can re-open the same hole. That file is NOT this worker's ownership and was not touched; it is reported as an open issue.
fix.residual_edge_case: A varp written back to 0 inside the window would be held and then skipped by 4b's `if (value == 0) continue;`. Harmless here — the player struct is memset at WorldPlayerInit and the loader writes varps directly, so an in-window write to 0 is already a no-op in ToriRSServer_WorldSetVarpOn. Recorded, not observed.

still_recorded_not_fixed: The general guard arguably belongs one line into ToriRSServer_Send (src/torirsserver/torirs_server_encode.c), so no future login-time writer can reopen the hole. The current guard covers the only emitter ever measured in that window.

A varp written back to 0 inside the reconnect window would be held and then skipped by WorldLoginFinish step 4b's `if (value == 0) continue;`. Harmless in practice, never observed, recorded rather than hidden.
No unit gate drives a reconnect, so a revert of the guard would not fail a test.
